Q1.headline: About 7 in 10: the court thinks it fairly likely that gold, bonds and bank credit stay central, with the new token rails built on top of them rather than replacing them.
up: Stablecoin supply passes $500B or 10% of T-bills while reserves stay in short bills, so more token money sits on Set 1 bonds
Central banks keep buying gold near the 2025 pace (863t) as sanctions reach more channels
The federal tax base starts moving to capital, energy or compute as the labor share falls
down: Treasury receipts stay wage-based while the labor share keeps falling from 52.8%, which weakens Treasuries as prime collateral in H2
A GENIUS amendment or the Basel crypto review lets non-Treasury assets back compliant tokens
Unsecured, income-underwritten lending on chain passes $50B by 2028
Q1.watch: Stablecoin reserve rules switch on 2027-01-18, then the stablecoin share of T-bills (4.3% now, tripwire 10%)

Q2.headline: About 2 in 3: likely that loans based on your future income stay with regulated lenders, while the old petrodollar recycling job passes to stablecoins.
up: Crypto-backed lending stays tiny next to bank loans (now $56.2B, about 0.4%)
Issuer attestations and TIC data show stablecoin demand is mostly new foreign dollar demand, not switching out of US deposits (Round 3 question R3-01)
down: Unsecured, income-underwritten lending on chain passes $50B, or the bank-funded share of consumer credit falls sharply by 2028
Stablecoin growth turns out to be mostly switching out of US money funds and bank deposits
Gulf Treasury holdings rise more than 20% in a year, a sign that old-style recycling is back
Q2.watch: Stablecoin supply against the tripwire of $500B or 10% of T-bills, with reserve rules live from 2027-01-18

Q3.headline: About 2 in 3: likely that crypto replaces how money moves but not what backs it, and that gold stays mainly a reserve for states rather than everyday money.
up: Compliant stablecoins keep gold out of their reserves (GENIUS lists no gold)
Tokenized gold stays a niche, now about $5.15B for XAUT plus PAXG, about 0.02% of the gold stock
down: Bill yields fall below about 1.5% and Congress widens stablecoin reserves to include gold (Round 3 question R3-10)
Clearing houses start accepting tokenized gold as margin
The Texas bullion-backed payment rail draws real volume after it opens
Q3.watch: Texas bullion-backed payments open 2027-05-01, and any amendment to GENIUS Sec. 4 on eligible reserves

Q4.headline: 8 in 10: very likely under current law that a UHI can count as income for a loan, but cannot be sold or pledged as a stream.
up: Any UHI bill keeps an anti-assignment clause like 42 USC 407 for Social Security
Lenders and Fannie Mae keep counting steady public income that continues at least 3 years
down: A US UHI or AI dividend bill makes the payments pledgeable or open to payroll-style deductions
Congress allows regulated borrowing against, or a business exception for, Trump Accounts
UHI amounts get reset each year by politicians, like Alaska's dividend, which makes them hard to underwrite
Q4.watch: Text of any US UHI or AI dividend bill: its CBO score and any assignment or deduction clauses (Round 3 question R3-08)

Q5.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that each country pays its own UHI from its own taxes, funds and currency, at very different real values.
up: More countries ration transfers with residency rules, as Macau did with 183 days for 2025
Emerging-market central banks answer dollar tokens with stablecoin limits, capital controls or their own digital currencies
down: A large printed UHI in a non-reserve currency keeps its real value for several years
US energy prices fall while dollar oil prices rise, which would mean the US privilege reaches further than the court allows
Q5.watch: Any US UHI bill that pays in dollar stablecoins, which would add dollarization pressure on weaker currencies

Q6.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that the route from first job to owning assets is still open at 18, but it has changed shape, with a broken housing rung and a crowded launch rung.
up: Unemployment for ages 20 to 24 keeps falling from 8.0%
Payment hours on a median home stay near 68, confirming the housing rung is the broken one
Child accounts or AI equity grants get funded at a scale that matters
down: A verified 1990 median home price more than 10% away from $92,000, or payment hours below 50 for 3 years
Asset returns beat wages, housing supply stays blocked and ownership grants stay token-sized into H1, which would make the gap permanent
The gap between graduate and all-worker unemployment widens as AI thins entry postings further
Q6.watch: NAR first-time buyer profile in November 2026 (median buyer age now a record 40)

Q7.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that the same arithmetic holds everywhere: a UHI's real value depends on how it is funded, and a digital token does not change that.
up: New transfers repeat the pattern: funded ones stay stable (Hong Kong), printed ones erode (Iran, Mongolia)
Calibrating the model's foreign absorption and overshoot inputs against IMF pass-through data confirms the country ranking
down: The interest paid on bank reserves is set near zero with no inflation response
A printed transfer above 5% of GDP runs with CPI below 2%
Q7.watch: The robot supply response (Round 3 question R3-02): nonfarm productivity sustained above 3%, and core services inflation as AI spreads

Q8.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that robots and cheap energy make products somewhat cheaper but brands barely, and that freight shocks shrink only slowly.
up: Store brands keep gaining share (a record 24% of units in H1 2026)
Electric trucks pass 5% of new class 8 truck sales
down: US battery cell capacity stays well under 20 GW by 2028, keeping electric freight tied to Chinese batteries
Platform take rates and ad prices fall sharply, which would make branded goods cheaper too
Q8.watch: EO 14421 rules due 24 December 2026, and US battery cell capacity against 20 GW by 2028

Q9.headline: About 2 in 3: likely that rivals' strongest card against the US plan is energy hardware, not currency, at least through 2028.
up: The 10 November 2026 suspension lapses so China's October 2025 rare-earth package takes effect, and the solar know-how ban is finalized
Yuan-financed panels and batteries flow to the Global South at scale
down: China drops its hardware controls for good while a Gulf state signs a yuan crude term contract
US battery cell capacity passes 20 GW by 2028 and China falls below 25% of US lithium-ion imports
Q9.watch: 10 November 2026, when China's rare-earth truce lapses or is renewed, then the final solar catalogue after 15 November

Q10.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that 'In Time' is wrong literally but partly right: goods got cheaper in hours of work, while homes, health cover and entry assets got dearer.
up: Payment hours on a median home stay near 68
New Fed wealth data keep showing owners capturing most of the gains
down: A verified 1990 median home price more than 10% away from $92,000, or payment hours below 50 for 3 years
The bottom half's equity share rises once child accounts are funded
Q10.watch: Fed distributional wealth data, next due about December 2026

M1.headline: 3 in 4: the court is fairly sure the interest on stablecoin reserves goes to issuers and distributors, not holders, and that the business breaks if bill yields fall near zero.
up: Next Circle results again show most reserve income paid to distributors (61.5% in Q2 2026)
If yields fall, issuers waive fees or fold into banks, as money funds did under zero rates
down: GENIUS is amended to allow yield to holders
Exchange rewards (3.75% in the model) are ruled legal at scale from 2027-01-18, passing most of the float to holders
M1.watch: Fed rate path and issuer earnings against the roughly 1.5% breakeven bill yield (10-year real yield 2.76% now)

M2.headline: 6 in 10, a lean: deposits mostly stay inside banks but get more expensive, and part of new money creation tilts from bank loans toward Treasury bills.
up: Stablecoins head toward TBAC's projected $2T by 2028, held mostly in bills
Deposit rates rise and banks keep shifting to funding nonbank lenders (loans to nonbanks up 19.9% to $2.06T)
down: Issuers park cash in money funds that use the Fed's reverse repo, so deposits really do leave the banking system
Stablecoin growth stalls well below $500B, which leaves the tilt toward bills small
M2.watch: Stablecoin share of T-bills (4.3% now, tripwire 10%) and Fed H.8 bank loans to nonbank lenders

M3.headline: 8 in 10: very likely an accurate snapshot of today. Gold is cheap for banks to own, costly to fund, and kept outside compliant dollar tokens.
up: Tether's Q3 2026 attestation confirms gold stays in USDT reserves, not in its compliant token USAT
Aave keeps a 0% loan to value on gold tokens on its main market
down: The Basel crypto review changes how gold or tokens are treated
A GENIUS amendment adds gold as an eligible reserve
The World Gold Council pooled gold pilot goes live and clearing houses accept tokenized gold as margin
M3.watch: Tether Q3 2026 attestation (gold tonnage, bill share), due about 31 October 2026

M4.headline: 6 in 10, a lean: a robot and solar economy shrinks the oil anchor, and the recycling job passes to stablecoins, Gulf equity in US AI and loans backed by energy assets.
up: Oil displaced by electric vehicles keeps growing toward the IEA's roughly 5 million barrels a day by 2030
Gulf funds keep buying US AI infrastructure, as in the MGX and BlackRock $40B Aligned deal
The UAE gets its swap line instead of turning to the yuan
down: A Gulf state signs a yuan term crude contract
Gulf Treasury holdings rise more than 20% in a year, meaning old-style recycling is back
A WTO or UNCTAD table puts oil's share of world trade well above the rough 5% used here
M4.watch: Outcome of the UAE swap line request, and FIMA repo use in the next crisis (Round 3 question R3-09)

M5.headline: 8 in 10: very likely that past cash transfers sort by how they were financed: small and funded stays safe, large and printed erodes within two to five years.
up: Singapore's vouchers, the one open gap, turn out to fit the funded pattern
New national transfers show the same split by financing
down: A large printed transfer in a floating non-reserve currency keeps its real value for five years
Re-analysis credits Mongolia's poverty fall to its 17.3% growth boom rather than the transfer
M5.watch: Research on Singapore's vouchers, the precedent Round 2 did not cover

M6.headline: Just over even: the toy model's ranking of countries is a fair lean, but its US inflation figures are a floor, not a forecast.
up: Calibrating foreign absorption and overshoot against IMF pass-through panels confirms the ranking
The measured robot supply response comes in near the model's strong case, where robots meet 80% of extra demand
down: Adding an interest rate channel reorders the countries (Japan's yen fell from about 110 to about 158 through rate gaps)
A printed transfer above 5% of GDP runs with CPI below 2%
M6.watch: Nonfarm productivity sustained above 3%, and PJM capacity prices, as clues to the robot supply response (Round 3 question R3-02)

M7.headline: About 85 in 100: the court is quite sure US law bars pledging or selling Social Security payments, and the record of abuse explains why.
up: Courts keep reading 42 USC 407 broadly, as the Supreme Court did in Philpott (1973)
Regulators keep acting against pension advance products
down: Congress makes a new UHI or benefit stream assignable
Evidence appears of a current, legal loan product secured by Alaska dividends
M7.watch: Assignment and deduction clauses in any US UHI or AI dividend bill (Round 3 question R3-08)

M8.headline: About 2 in 3: likely that a token balance you already received can be pledged in DeFi, but a future UHI stream only if the payer designs it that way.
up: Token UHI pilots copy Shenzhen-style rules: not transferable, spendable only at listed shops, unspent money recovered
The US ban on a retail digital dollar holds, so any token UHI rides on private stablecoins that pay holders no yield
down: A permissive issuer makes the UHI stream a transferable streaming-payment token
Unsecured, income-underwritten lending on chain passes $50B
M8.watch: Token-payment provisions in any US UHI bill, and the CBDC ban expiry on 2030-12-31

M9.headline: 8 in 10: very likely that the entry job market is soft but not collapsing. AI as the main cause is rated lower, at 55.
up: Next BLS releases keep unemployment for ages 20 to 24 near 8%
NY Fed data keep showing recent graduates above the all-worker rate (5.6% against 4.2%)
down: Unemployment for ages 20 to 24 climbs back above the 9.2% of a year earlier
Entry postings in AI-exposed jobs fall well below the current 44.7% share
M9.watch: The gap between recent-graduate and all-worker unemployment, about 1.4 points now

M10.headline: 6 in 10, a lean: AI cuts the cost of starting a business, but not the odds of success, so it offsets the underclass meme only for the top tail.
up: Ad prices and platform fees keep rising faster than production costs fall (Round 3 question R3-07)
Top-tenth solo founders keep pulling away from the median (61 times in 2025)
down: Median solo-founder revenue rises two years running while ad prices fall
Solo founders win a growing share of priced-round money (14.7% now)
M10.watch: Meta's average price per ad in its 10-Q filings, and whether Amazon removes its 3.5% surcharge

M11.headline: 8 in 10: very likely that the Trump Account rules are as stated, and that the values follow from plain compounding on the stated returns.
up: IRS rules stay unchanged as the first seeded cohort grows toward 18 in 2043
Treasury data by income confirm that family contributions, not the seed, drive balances
down: Congress adds a business start-up withdrawal exception or allows borrowing against the account
Real returns over 18 years land below the table's 3% low case
M11.watch: Treasury data on contributions by income, and any AI equity routed into Trump Accounts (Round 3 question R3-11)

M12.headline: About 7 in 10: likely that past mobility windows reopened when non-owners got a large asset or credential paired with credit. Whether a modern version works is less certain.
up: The Goldin and Katz high school figures, now from memory, are verified
A modern program that pairs a large grant with credit shows mobility gains
down: Evidence that a past window reopened without a large asset or credential
Large modern grants fail to move the bottom half's equity share
M12.watch: Fed distributional wealth data, next due about December 2026, for any move in the bottom half's equity share

M13.headline: 3 in 4: fairly sure that making the product is a small part of a cosmetic's price, and that robots cut factory costs but not retailer or platform cuts.
up: Next filings keep marketing near a quarter of net sales at e.l.f. and Estee Lauder
Ad prices keep rising as cheap AI creative floods the auctions
down: Retailer margins or platform take rates fall sharply
Robot savings show up as large shelf-price cuts in branded goods
M13.watch: Amazon's seller-services share of sales and Meta's average price per ad (Round 3 question R3-07)

M14.headline: About 7 in 10: the 2026 freight prices are confirmed, while the timelines for driverless and electric freight are only plausible.
up: Aurora reaches about 200 driverless trucks by end 2026
Tesla Semi deliveries scale up after the September 2026 start
down: Timelines slip again, as when Tesla dropped its 2026 volume forecast
The IMO carbon framework session pencilled for 2026-12-04 slips or fails
M14.watch: IMO carbon framework session pencilled for 2026-12-04, and Aurora's driverless truck count at end 2026

M15.headline: Just over even: attention, distribution and trust are what sell, but a cash price premium for 'human-made' is not yet proven.
up: A controlled study finds a measurable price premium for human-made or founder-trusted goods
AI content labeling rules make human-made claims verifiable
down: Retailers keep cloning what works (store brands at a record 24% unit share)
Marketplace data with provenance labels show no price premium
M15.watch: Marketplace price data with provenance labels, and any AI labeling rules (Round 3 question R3-06)

M16.headline: About 2 in 3: the ranking that puts hardware levers (threat 3.20, 3.20 and 3.00) far above money levers (0.12 for a BRICS currency) is a fair judgment, but it is judgment, not data.
up: Rare-earth controls return when the 10 November 2026 suspension lapses
The critical minerals ban suspended to 27 November 2026 comes back into force
down: A Gulf state signs a yuan crude term contract
China speeds up Treasury sales well beyond the gradual run-down from $694B to $590.7B
M16.watch: 10 and 27 November 2026, the two supply-chain suspension dates

M17.headline: 3 in 4: fairly sure that time prices split cleanly, with traded goods cheaper in hours of work and assets and local services dearer, and that owners captured most dollar gains.
up: Verified 1990 inputs (home and car prices) match the memory figures
The next Fed wealth release keeps the top 0.1% share rising (15.0% in 2026 Q2)
down: A verified 1990 median home price more than 10% away from $92,000
Wages outrun home and health costs in hours of work for several years
M17.watch: Verification of the 1990 median existing-home price ($92,000), the single input both lanes rest on

M18.headline: About 2 in 3: likely that the US exports inflation only when the dollar is strong, and that in 2026 it is not insulated itself.
up: Oil-importing allies keep spending to defend their currencies (Japan spent about $170B to $175B)
US energy prices keep rising with world oil prices
down: US energy prices fall while dollar oil prices rise
The 2026 currency falls in Asia turn out to be mostly an oil shock rather than a dollar shock
M18.watch: USD/JPY near the 160 to 164 intervention zone, and Japan's next intervention
